title: Exercise 3: When the file is missing
lessonSummary: Well done! You catch FileNotFoundError and check with os whether a file exists.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: a missing file, exists and remove.
tasks.codeTemplate:
import os
try:
    with open("missing.txt", "r") as f:
        print(f.read())

    f.write("Stable book of the farm\n")
print("Exists:", os.path.exists("stable_book.txt"))
os.remove("stable_book.txt")
print("Afterwards:", os.path.exists("stable_book.txt"))

title: Exercise 6: CSV tables: writer and reader
lessonSummary: Masterful! You write and read tables in CSV format.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: write CSV, read it and calculate.
tasks.codeTemplate:
import csv
with open("horses.csv", "w", newline="") as f:
    w = csv.writer(f)
    w.writerow(["name", "age"])
    w.writerow(["Blitz", 8])
    w.writerow(["Storm", 12])
    w.writerow(["Luna", 6])
total = 0
with open("horses.csv", "r") as f:
    r = csv.reader(f)
    next(r)
    for row in r:
        total += int(row[1])
print("Total:", total)

title: Exercise 7: CSV with DictReader and switching formats
lessonSummary: World class! You read tables as dictionaries and convert between JSON and CSV.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: DictWriter and DictReader.

import csv
horses = [
    {"name": "Blitz", "breed": "Hanoverian", "age": 8, "points": 120},
    {"name": "Storm", "breed": "Haflinger", "age": 12, "points": 150},
    {"name": "Luna", "breed": "Icelandic", "age": 6, "points": 90},
]
with open("horses.csv", "w", newline="") as f:
